passage: Emeka strolled down the corridor, ready to make his usual joke about Wei's glasses, and Wei flinched. His shoulders jumped up and his books rose against his chest like a shield. Emeka's grin faltered. He had expected to feel big; instead his stomach turned. Behind him his friends were waiting for the punchline. "It's just a joke," he began, and heard how false it sounded. Wei had already backed against the lockers. So Emeka dropped his voice. "Sorry, Wei. I'm not going to say it. I shouldn't have said it before, either." Wei only looked at him, unsure. Emeka walked away, red in the face.

qa.q: Where was Wei standing when Emeka apologised?
qa.a: Wei had already backed against the lockers.

qa.q: What was Emeka feeling when he saw Wei flinch?
qa.a: His grin faltered and his stomach turned, so he felt uncomfortable and ashamed instead of the big feeling he expected.

qa.q: What did Emeka's apology get right, and what might he still need to do?
qa.a: He stopped, admitted he should not have said it before, and did not call it a joke; he may need to keep his word over the coming days so Wei can feel safe.

qa.q: How might Wei see Emeka's apology?
qa.a: Wei looked unsure, which suggests he may not trust it yet after being teased, and he may need time to see that Emeka means it.

grounding: A teaser sees the target's fear, feels uncomfortable instead of proud, and stops and says sorry.

passage:
At the swimming club, Lalit liked calling Pranav "the drowning fish" whenever Pranav paused at the shallow end. The other boys snorted. It felt like a joke.
On Saturday, Lalit walked up behind him in the changing room. Pranav jumped and pressed himself against the lockers, eyes wide.
Lalit stopped. He had meant to say something funny. Instead a cold feeling crept up his neck. Pranav was scared of him. Not laughing. Scared.
After practice, Lalit found him by the vending corner. "Pranav, I'm sorry. For the fish thing. All of it. I'll stop." He meant it.
Pranav nodded slowly. The next Saturday, nobody called him a fish.

qa.q: What did Lalit call Pranav at the swimming club?
What was Lalit feeling when Pranav pressed against the lockers?
qa.a: He felt uncomfortable and shaken, a cold feeling creeping up his neck as he realised Pranav was scared of him.

qa.q: Why was Lalit's apology better than calling it a joke?
qa.a: He saw the fear was real, said sorry and meant it, and then actually stopped, which ended the hurt.

qa.q: How might Pranav see Lalit coming up behind him?
qa.a: Pranav sees him as a threat, jumping and pressing himself against the lockers.

grounding: A boy sees the boy he teases flinch in fear; instead of feeling proud he feels uncomfortable, stops and apologises sincerely.

passage:
Monday. Tushar tapped Jatin on the head with a rolled-up notebook as he passed. "Morning, egghead!" Jatin ducked. Tushar grinned. It was just a joke.
Wednesday. Tushar lifted his hand to wave at a friend, and Jatin flinched, covering his head. Tushar saw it. His grin slid away. He felt sick. Was that because of me?
That evening he told himself it was nothing. But he kept seeing Jatin's arms over his head.
Friday. Before class, Tushar went to Jatin's desk. "I'm sorry I kept doing that. It wasn't a joke for you. I'm stopping." Jatin looked at him for a long moment, then gave a small nod.

qa.q: What did Tushar hit Jatin with on Monday?
How did Tushar feel when Jatin flinched on Wednesday?
qa.a: He felt sick and uneasy, wondering if Jatin's fear was because of him.

qa.q: What mature step did Tushar take on Friday?
qa.a: He apologised directly, admitted it wasn't a joke for Jatin, and said he would stop.

qa.q: How might Jatin have felt when Tushar raised his hand on Wednesday?
qa.a: Jatin felt afraid, expecting to be hit, which is why he flinched and covered his head.

grounding: A boy sees the boy he teases flinch in fear, feels uncomfortable rather than proud, and apologises sincerely instead of calling it a joke.
